A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STI-Bench. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends with references; v4 additionally contains readable Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven MLLMs on STI-Bench in Tables 2–3 and an analysis of sampled Gemini-2.5-Pro errors.

after.justification: v4 reports evaluations of ten MLLMs, retains the error analysis, and adds original subgroup results in Appendix C, Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: The eight-task benchmark and its ground-truth/QA-generation pipeline are retained. v4 elaborates trajectory processing and distractor scaling without establishing an algorithmic redesign. The explicit frame-sampling revision concerns evaluation settings.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waymo, ScanNet, and Omni6DPose for the same outdoor, indoor, and desktop coverage, with eight tasks and 2,064 QA pairs. v4's finer category breakdowns analyze the retained benchmark rather than establish added datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 expand the evaluated comparator set from seven to ten models by adding MiniCPM-V-2.6, VideoChat-Flash, and VideoChat-R1. All seven previously evaluated models remain, substantially broadening the open-source comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated sampling protocol from 1 fps to 30 uniformly sampled frames per record, with a 20-frame exception for Claude-3.7-Sonnet. v4 also states that sampling FPS is supplied in the prompt. These changes affect the information available during evaluation; five-option accuracy scoring remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds descriptive subgroup analyses for four models by outdoor lighting/weather, indoor room type, and desktop material. These extend v1's coarse scene comparisons and error taxonomy. Figures 11–12 provide fuller traces for the two cases already summarized in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for model accuracy. The approximately 200 sampled error records are described in both versions.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace scores throughout the retained model set. Table 2's leader changes from Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 40.8%, ahead of Gemini-2.5-Pro at 40.5%, to Gemini at 41.4%, ahead of Qwen at 40.7%. These are results under revised sampling, not established same-setting gains. v4 also adds three models' results and subgroup scores, while introducing conflicting GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-Flash totals between Tables 2 and 3.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix B add an explicit derivation of the shared distractor-adjustment weight from a target minimum answer gap and state the resulting gap-preservation property. v1 describes scaling qualitatively. Appendix A mostly supplies standard formulas for existing tasks; no substantial theoretical framework is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a quantitative spatial-temporal benchmark spanning three environments and evidence that current MLLMs struggle with precise physical understanding. The same three principal weaknesses remain. Updated concluding accuracy figures support this retained claim.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 add model specialization and architectural differences as possible explanations for scene-dependent performance. v4 also emphasizes Gemini's relative strength in quantitative tasks despite low absolute accuracy. The established error mechanisms and limitations for embodied applications remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands construction documentation: exact distractor intervals of 0.5–5 cm, 5–50 cm, and 0.5–5 m; sampling and adjustment formulas; annotation conversion and ground-truth conventions; RDP trajectory simplification; and approximately 20% QA retention after review. It also adds a project-page link. These mostly disclose previously unspecified implementation details rather than demonstrate changed construction settings.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for MiniCPM-V, VideoChat-Flash, VideoChat-R1, and the Gemini 2.5 Pro preview model card. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing spatial and video benchmarks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in distractor adjustment, experimental settings, and result interpretation. v4 adds acknowledgements and Appendices A–C, alongside small language corrections. The main section sequence and most introductory, related-work, task-definition, and error-analysis prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 reorganizes columns to correctly group static and dynamic tasks, and Tables 2–3 expand and reorder model rows. Figures 1, 5, and 7 are redrawn with revised labels, legends, or styling. The appendix adds three tables and five figures, including expanded displays of the existing reasoning examples.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative construction account, v4 supplies concrete calibration and annotation details and corrects Table 2's task grouping, improving auditability and interpretation. Broader model and subgroup comparisons add useful evidence. However, newly conflicting totals across Tables 2–3—GPT-4o at 34.8% versus 35.2%, and Gemini-2.0-Flash at 38.7% versus 36.0%—weaken confidence in precise rankings and limit the overall gain.
